priorStories.headline: Grand jury rejects charges against Cassidy Hutchinson
priorStories.body:
A federal grand jury in Washington declined prosecutors’ request to indict former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson over allegations that she lied to Congress about President Donald Trump’s actions surrounding the January 6, 2021, Capitol attack. The proposed charges have not been made public.

Hutchinson says she stands by her testimony. The Justice Department did not immediately comment.

sources.name: ABC News via ABC7 Los Angeles

priorStories.headline: Israeli exit polls show no majority
priorStories.body:
Voting ended in Israel’s Knesset election, and exit polls from the major television broadcasters projected that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot had won the 61 seats needed for a majority.

Likud was projected to remain the largest party, but official results were still pending. Forming a government could depend on coalition negotiations lasting several weeks.

candidates.summary: A high-speed train struck the rear of another train that had stopped near Urda in Spain’s Toledo province, derailing two cars. Authorities reported at least 64 deaths and about 80 injuries as rescue work continued. The two trains carried more than 500 passengers in total and were traveling from Madrid toward Seville. The cause remained under investigation, and rail service between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia was suspended.
candidates.title: Spain train collision kills at least 64

candidates.summary: Official returns from Israel’s election continued to show no governing majority. With about 85% of votes counted, Likud had 20.8%, Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar had 16.1%, and Arab-led parties collectively had 14.9%. Local projections assigned 53 seats to Likud and its allies, 48 to Yashar’s bloc and 19 to Arab-led parties, making the latter potentially decisive in coalition talks. Roughly half a million absentee ballots remained to be counted.
candidates.title: Israeli count leaves Arab-led parties holding potential balance
